# Configuration

lt-suite reads one TOML file. Every key has a default, so a config holds only what
differs from the defaults. The `lt-suite-setup` skill writes the file for you; this
page lists what it can contain.

## Where the file lives

Lookup order, first hit wins:

1. `--config <path>` on any script.
2. The `LT_SUITE_CONFIG` environment variable.
3. `./lt-suite.toml` in the current folder. Sandboxed agents that can write only in
   their workspace use this one; setup proposes it when a probe fails (below).
4. The platform file:
   - Linux: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/lt-suite/config.toml`
   - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/lt-suite/config.toml`
   - Windows: `%APPDATA%\lt-suite\config.toml`
5. No file: built-in defaults only. A script that needs a setting with no default,
   such as `lt.origin`, exits 3 with
   `lt.origin is not set. Run the lt-suite-setup skill or set it in <path>.`

`setup.py locate` (and `python3 -m ltcore.config locate`) checks whether the platform
config folder and data folder are writable and whether a loopback port can be bound.
When any check fails it proposes `./lt-suite.toml` with
`paths.data_dir = ".lt-suite/data"`, `browser.transport = "download"` and
`paths.downloads_mode = "copy"`.

## How values combine

The effective config is `shared/config.defaults.toml`, then
`shared/style.defaults.toml` (palettes and fonts), then your file. Tables merge key by
key; an array (including `[[tiers.tier]]` and `[[text_cleaners]]`) replaces the default
array whole. An unknown key is an error, so a typo cannot pass silently.

Relative paths in your file resolve against the file's own folder, and `~` expands.
`curriculum.learning_outcomes_file` resolves against `curriculum.root`.
`paths.captures_dir` and `paths.runs_dir` are folders inside the data folder unless
they are absolute. An empty string means "unset": the default or the feature is off.

## Writing the file

The setup skill writes the config through `ltcore.config.write()`: it validates the
values, writes to a temporary file and renames it into place, refuses to replace an
existing file without `--force`, and keeps the replaced file as `<name>.bak`.
`--stdout` prints the TOML instead of writing it (claude.ai chat, where a file in the
container is lost at the end of the session).

## Environment variables

| Name | Effect |
|---|---|
| `LT_SUITE_CONFIG` | config file path |
| `LT_SUITE_DATA` | data folder (runs, captures, state, approvals, fonts, venv); wins over `paths.data_dir` |
| `LT_SUITE_CACHE` | cache folder (derived themes, static font instances); wins over `paths.cache_dir` |
| `LT_SUITE_NO_INSTALL` | `1` makes `export_module.py --install` refuse (evaluation guard) |

No other variable is read. Every message that names a path also names where it came
from: `flag`, `env LT_SUITE_DATA`, `config paths.data_dir` or `default`.

## Data folder

`$LT_SUITE_DATA`, else `paths.data_dir`, else the platform default:
Linux `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/lt-suite`, macOS
`~/Library/Application Support/lt-suite/data`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lt-suite\data`.

```
<data>/captures/            module-<id>.json, reference-<id>.json, media/
<data>/incoming/            the capture sink writes here; stamp_capture.py moves files on
<data>/runs/<module_id>/    run.json, logs/, fill-js/, fill-report.json, approvals.json,
                            page-kinds.json, check-answer.json, reconcile-worklist.json,
                            fill-report-pre-rat.json, reconciled.json,
                            model-answer.json
<data>/state/               calibration.json, ledger.json, applied.json
<data>/lexicon/             lexicon entries proposed by run review
<data>/fonts/               fonts fetched by setup
<data>/venv/                Python environment when the directory is outside git work trees
```

The bootstrap environment uses `<data>/venv` when its resolved path has no git
work tree ancestor. Otherwise it uses the platform data folder's `venv/`. Setup and
runtime lookup resolve symlinks, check the final environment folder and reject both
locations when neither is outside a git work tree.

## Cache folder

`$LT_SUITE_CACHE`, else `paths.cache_dir`, else Linux `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/lt-suite`,
macOS `~/Library/Caches/lt-suite`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lt-suite\cache`. It holds
`themes/` and `font-cache/`; deleting it costs only recomputation.

## Command line

With `shared/` (in the repository) or a skill's `scripts/_shared/` on `PYTHONPATH`:

```
python3 -m ltcore.config path                 # which file is used, and why
python3 -m ltcore.config validate [--config F]
python3 -m ltcore.config show [--origins]     # effective config; --origins names each key's source
python3 -m ltcore.config get fill.max_pages_per_call
python3 -m ltcore.config locate               # probes and proposal, as JSON
python3 -m ltcore.config write --from answers.toml [--force] [--stdout]
python3 -m ltcore.store                       # the data and cache layout
```

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 invalid, refused or unknown key, 2 usage, 3 missing config file or
unset key (`get` on a key whose value is `""` or `[]`).

## Examples

- `examples/configs/minimal.toml`: the smallest working config.
- `examples/usyd-md/config.toml`: every institution key filled for University of Sydney, Doctor of Medicine (MD), with unit code `MDMP5512` as a label, dotted week numbering (block week and session), learning-outcome headings that carry that number, and 4 source tiers: Course material: lecture slides, transcripts, learning outcomes, practical and TBL material for the week; eTG Complete (Therapeutic Guidelines); Clinical practice guidance from a named institution; Recent peer-reviewed evidence (DOI or PMID). Public programme values only; replace its placeholder paths with your own. `examples/usyd-md/README.md` explains each value.
## Keys

### `schema_version`

Config format version. This release reads version 1.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | int | `1` | Config format version. This release reads version 1. |

### `institution`

Who the config is for. Labels only; nothing here gates a run.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `institution.profile` | str | `"generic"` | Free label recorded in run.json. |
| `institution.name` | str | `""` | Institution and programme name, for display only. |
| `institution.unit_code` | str | `""` | Optional unit or course code recorded in run.json. No gate reads it. |
| `institution.locale` | str | `"en"` | Spelling and synonym set used by the diagram consistency checks. One of: `en`, `en-AU`, `en-GB`, `en-US`. |
| `institution.timezone` | str | `""` | IANA time zone name, for example Europe/London. Empty means the system zone. |

### `lt`

The Lt address the capture and fill skills may open.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lt.origin` | str | `""` | Lt address, https://<tenant>.lt.app, with no path. Capture and fill refuse to run while it is empty. |
| `lt.instance` | str | `""` | Optional Lt instance id. Empty means read it from the page URL. |
| `lt.allowed_url_patterns` | list[str] | `[]` | URL patterns for the browser server's --allowedUrlPattern option, shown in the setup docs. |

### `paths`

Where lt-suite keeps its files.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths.data_dir` | str | `""` | Data folder for runs, captures, state, fonts and the venv. Empty means LT_SUITE_DATA, then the platform default. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `paths.captures_dir` | str | `"captures"` | Captured modules and references. Folder; relative to the data folder. |
| `paths.runs_dir` | str | `"runs"` | Per-module run folders. Folder; relative to the data folder. |
| `paths.downloads_dir` | str | `""` | Browser download folder for the download transport. Empty means the platform Downloads folder. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `paths.downloads_mode` | str | `"move"` | move or copy files out of the download folder. Use copy when a sandbox cannot delete outside the workspace. One of: `move`, `copy`. |
| `paths.cache_dir` | str | `""` | Cache folder for derived themes and font instances. Empty means LT_SUITE_CACHE, then the platform default. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |

### `notes`

The notes graph that export writes pages into.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notes.graph_path` | str | `""` | Notes graph root folder. Empty turns every notes output off. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `notes.format` | str | `"logseq"` | Page format: logseq, obsidian or markdown. One of: `logseq`, `obsidian`, `markdown`. |
| `notes.pages_dir` | str | `"pages"` | Pages folder inside the graph. |
| `notes.assets_dir` | str | `"assets"` | Assets folder inside the graph. |
| `notes.whiteboards_dir` | str | `"whiteboards"` | Whiteboards folder inside the graph. |
| `notes.page_namespace` | str | `"Lt"` | Namespace of exported module pages. |
| `notes.page_title` | str | `"{namespace}/{week} {title}"` | Page title template. Placeholders: {namespace}, {week}, {title}, {module_id}. |
| `notes.file_name_format` | str | `"triple-lowbar"` | Logseq file name format; triple-lowbar is Logseq's default for new graphs. One of: `triple-lowbar`, `legacy`. |
| `notes.stamp_property` | str | `"lt-module"` | Page property that marks a page as lt-suite module output. Drafting skips stamped pages. |

### `curriculum`

The course material tree the answer skill reads as Tier 1.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curriculum.root` | str | `""` | Course material folder. Empty turns week lookup off. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `curriculum.learning_outcomes_file` | str | `""` | Learning outcomes file. Path; relative to `curriculum.root`. |
| `curriculum.skip_dirs` | list[str] | `[]` | Folder names under curriculum.root that never hold week folders. |
| `curriculum.text_extensions` | list[str] | `[".md", ".txt", ".vtt", ".pdf", ".pptx", ".docx"]` | File types counted as course text. |
| `curriculum.week_number_pattern` | str | `'(?i)\bweek\s*(\d{1,2})\b'` | Regular expression that finds the week in a module title. The first capture group is the week; an optional second group is the session. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |
| `curriculum.week_dir_pattern` | str | `'^(?i:week\s*)?{num}(?:\D\|$)'` | Regular expression for a week folder name; {num} is replaced by the escaped week number. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |
| `curriculum.title_stopwords` | list[str] | `[]` | Extra words ignored when matching a title to a folder. |
| `curriculum.patterns.lesson` | str | `'(?i)\blesson\s*(\d+)'` | Regular expression for a lesson number in a module title. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |
| `curriculum.patterns.bare_number` | str | `'^\d+$'` | Regular expression for a title that is only a number. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |
| `curriculum.patterns.ilo_heading` | str | `'(?i)^#+\s*learning outcomes?\b'` | Regular expression for a heading in the learning outcomes file. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |
| `curriculum.patterns.ilo_kind` | str | `""` | Regular expression for the kind line under a learning-outcome heading. Empty means none. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |

### `rat`

Readiness assurance tests (individual iRAT and team tRAT).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rat.answers_dir` | str | `""` | A folder of your RAT sheets. Only page_kinds.py and fill read immediate files when policy or a current choice allows it. Empty means no folder. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `rat.irat` | str | `"skip"` | Individual RAT: skip, ask each time, or enter your own sheet with from_dir. Never drafted. One of: `skip`, `ask`, `from_dir`. |
| `rat.trat` | str | `"ask"` | Team RAT: from_dir enters your sheets, ask requests a choice, skip leaves the page. One of: `from_dir`, `ask`, `skip`. |
| `rat.answers_dirs` | list[str] | `[]` | More RAT answer-sheet folders with the same read and quarantine rules. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `rat.kind_markers.trat` | str | `'(?i)\b[tg]-?RAT\b\|\b(?:team\|group) readiness\b'` | Marks a trat from content text only. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |
| `rat.kind_markers.irat` | str | `'(?i)\bi-?RAT\b\|\bindividual readiness\b'` | Marks a irat from content text only. Must compile as a Python regular expression. |

### `model_answer`

Lt's model answer in page data.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_answer.read` | bool | `true` | Read Lt's panelState.modelAnswer from page data into the run folder. false turns it off; module.json never carries it. |

### `tiers`

Provenance tiers for drafted answers, in order.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tiers.tier` | array of tables | see below | Source tiers in search order. |
| `tiers.tier[].id` | int |  | Tier number. Required. |
| `tiers.tier[].label` | str |  | What the tier holds. Required. |
| `tiers.tier[].tag_template` | str |  | Provenance tag template, for example [T2:{issuer}:{topic}]. Required. |
| `tiers.tier[].requires_accessed` | bool | `false` | The tag must record the date the source was read. |
| `tiers.tier[].issuer_order` | list[str] | `[]` | Preferred issuers, nearest first. |
| `tiers.tier[].access_note` | str | `""` | How the user reaches this tier's sources. |
| `tiers.reference_set` | list[str] | `[]` | Reference works the user trusts. |
| `tiers.fallback_sources` | list[str] | `[]` | Ordered search list after Tier 1. |
| `tiers.framing` | str | `""` | Jurisdiction framing sentence for drafted answers. |

Default for `tiers.tier`:

```toml
[[tiers.tier]]
id = 1
label = "Course material (slides, transcripts, learning outcomes)"
tag_template = "[T1:{source}]"
requires_accessed = false
issuer_order = []
access_note = ""

[[tiers.tier]]
id = 2
label = "Licensed reference or guideline service"
tag_template = "[T2:{issuer}:{topic}]"
requires_accessed = true
issuer_order = []
access_note = ""

[[tiers.tier]]
id = 3
label = "Published clinical or institutional guidance"
tag_template = "[T3:{issuer}:{topic}]"
requires_accessed = false
issuer_order = []
access_note = ""

[[tiers.tier]]
id = 4
label = "Peer-reviewed literature (DOI or PMID)"
tag_template = "[T4:{doi_or_pmid}]"
requires_accessed = false
issuer_order = []
access_note = ""
```

### `pdf`

PDF output settings.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `pdf.strip_metadata` | bool | `true` | Run the built-in metadata strip on every PDF. |

### `style`

Palettes. Defaults live in shared/style.defaults.toml.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style.palettes` | list[str] | `["tol-bright", "petroff-10-on-primer-dark-high-contrast"]` | Palette catalog ids; every final export is made once per palette. |
| `style.print_palette` | str | `"tol-bright"` | Light palette for print and PDF submission. |
| `style.custom_palettes_file` | str | `""` | TOML file of user palettes with the same roles as the catalog. Empty means none. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |

### `fonts`

Fonts. Base keys apply to every output. Per-output keys replace the base family and file keys for that role. Empty labels inherit PDF sans, then base sans.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fonts.sans` | str | `"Noto Sans"` | Sans family name from the font catalog, or a file path. Overridden by nonempty fonts.pdf.sans or fonts.diagram.sans or fonts.labels.sans. |
| `fonts.mono` | str | `"Noto Sans Mono"` | Mono family name from the font catalog, or a file path. Overridden by nonempty fonts.pdf.mono or fonts.diagram.mono. |
| `fonts.sans_path` | str | `""` | Explicit sans font file. Empty means resolve fonts.sans. Ignored when the output sets this role. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `fonts.mono_path` | str | `""` | Explicit mono font file. Empty means resolve fonts.mono. Ignored when the output sets this role. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `fonts.mono_bold_path` | str | `""` | Explicit bold mono font file. Empty means resolve fonts.mono. Ignored when the output sets this role. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `fonts.text_px` | int | `14` | Diagram node text size in px. |
| `fonts.allow_download` | bool | `true` | Setup may fetch catalog fonts into the data folder, after the user says yes. |
| `fonts.page_fonts` | str | `"local"` | local embeds fonts in HTML and drawio files; google keeps the Google Fonts link. google needs Google-hosted families; doctor warns about others. One of: `local`, `google`. |
| `fonts.system_fallback` | bool | `true` | Use SF Pro / SF Mono on macOS, Segoe UI / Cascadia Mono on Windows, or DejaVu on Linux after Noto fails, for page PDFs and labels. System fonts are never bundled, cut or web-embedded. |
| `fonts.pdf.sans` | str | `""` | Sans family or font file for pdf. Set values replace base family and path keys for this role. Empty inherits base keys. |
| `fonts.pdf.mono` | str | `""` | Mono family or font file for pdf. Set values replace base family and path keys for this role. Empty inherits base keys. |
| `fonts.diagram.sans` | str | `""` | Sans family or font file for diagram. Set values replace base family and path keys for this role. Empty inherits base keys. |
| `fonts.diagram.mono` | str | `""` | Mono family or font file for diagram. Set values replace base family and path keys for this role. Empty inherits base keys. |
| `fonts.labels.sans` | str | `""` | Sans family or font file for labels. Set values replace base family and path keys for this role. Empty inherits PDF sans, then base sans. annotate.font_path wins. |

### `browser`

How skills reach the signed-in browser.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `browser.adapter` | str | `"auto"` | Browser tool used to run page scripts. auto, chrome-devtools-mcp and antigravity start lt-chrome; claude-in-chrome, playwright-mcp and manual-paste make lt-chrome serve no tools. A workspace lt-suite.toml cannot start lt-chrome when the platform config chose a quiet adapter. Restart the agent after a change. One of: `auto`, `claude-in-chrome`, `chrome-devtools-mcp`, `playwright-mcp`, `antigravity`, `manual-paste`. |
| `browser.transport` | str | `"sink"` | Capture output route: sink (loopback POST) or download. One of: `sink`, `download`. |
| `browser.sink_port` | int | `8731` | Loopback port of the capture sink. |
| `browser.lib_mode` | str | `"inline"` | Fill scripts carry the library inline or load it from the loopback server. One of: `inline`, `served`. |
| `browser.lib_port` | int | `8733` | Loopback port of the fill library server. |
| `browser.js_tmp_dir` | str | `""` | Folder for rendered page scripts. Empty means the OS temp folder's lt-suite-js-<uid>/ (mode 0700, checked on every render). Setup records the folder that worked. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `browser.chromium` | str | `"chrome"` | Chromium browser lt-chrome attaches to with auto-connect. Chrome channels use Chrome's own profile folder; the others use the folder listed in docs/browser-adapters.md; other needs browser.chromium_user_data_dir. One of: `chrome`, `chrome-beta`, `chrome-dev`, `chrome-canary`, `chromium`, `edge`, `brave`, `vivaldi`, `other`. |
| `browser.chromium_user_data_dir` | str | `""` | The browser's user data folder: the parent of the Profile Path shown at chrome://version. Empty means the folder for browser.chromium. Used by auto-connect only. Relative paths resolve against the config file; ~ expands. Control characters, double quotes, percent and exclamation marks are refused. Path; relative to the config file's folder. |
| `browser.devtools_url` | str | `""` | Empty: lt-chrome auto-connects after you turn on remote debugging at chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging. Set: lt-chrome attaches to a browser you started with --remote-debugging-port and its own --user-data-dir. Only http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://[::1]:<port>, with port 1 to 65535, is accepted. |

### `fill`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fill.approval_mode` | str | `"manual"` | manual, auto or skip-all. Boundary pages always need manual. One of: `manual`, `auto`, `skip-all`. |
| `fill.max_pages_per_call` | int | `5` | Most pages filled per browser call. Values above 1 apply only after the origin's cross-page calibration passes. |
| `fill.save_wait.quiet_ms` | int | `300` | No request in flight for this long after every key is saved. |
| `fill.save_wait.max_ms` | int | `20000` | Cap counted from the last write; reaching it returns unconfirmed. |
| `fill.save_wait.fallback_ms` | int | `4000` | Uncalibrated rule: wait at least this long after the last write. |
| `fill.save_wait.render_wait_ms` | int | `5000` | Categories panel render wait. |
| `fill.dialog.max_ms` | int | `15000` | Confirm-dialog cap. |
| `fill.dialog.fallback_ms` | int | `6000` | Confirm-dialog wait when uncalibrated. |
| `fill.check_answer.enabled` | bool | `false` | Press Lt's Check Answer on eligible multi-attempt items after their drafts are written and verified, and change each answer until Lt marks it correct or locks it, or no untried answer remains. Never on single-attempt items or on pages classified as team or individual tests. Setup asks. |

### `text_cleaners`

External text or file cleaners run on outputs. Each entry: name, stage, argv, timeout_s.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text_cleaners` | array of tables | `[]` | External text or file cleaners run on outputs. Each entry: name, stage, argv, timeout_s. |
| `text_cleaners[].name` | str |  | Label shown in logs. Required. |
| `text_cleaners[].stage` | str |  | fill-text, pdf or diagram. One of: `fill-text`, `pdf`, `diagram`. Required. |
| `text_cleaners[].argv` | list[str] |  | Command and arguments. fill-text and diagram use {in} and {out}; pdf uses {pdf}. Required. |
| `text_cleaners[].timeout_s` | int | `60` | Seconds before the cleaner is stopped. |

| `diagram.illustration.credit` | str | `""` | Credit line for inset illustrations. Empty means none. |
| `diagram.treatment_check.provider_label` | str | `"treatment guideline"` | Name of the guideline source in messages. |
| `diagram.treatment_check.ledger_name` | str | `"guideline-ledger.json"` | Ledger file name in the case folder. |
| `diagram.anki.tag_prefix` | str | `"Diagram::"` | Tag prefix for diagram flashcards. |
| `diagram.layout.workers` | str | `"auto"` | auto uses fork on POSIX and serial elsewhere; serial or a worker count. |

### `capture`

Capture skill.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capture.drop_text_patterns` | list[str] | `["^Copyright ©"]` | Regular expressions for author text dropped from captures. |
| `capture.timeouts.post_ms` | int | `30000` | Timeout for one POST to the sink. |

### `improvement`

Run review and the improvement loop.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `improvement.benchmark_cells` | list[str] | `[]` | Benchmark cells the improvement loop compares before and after a change. |
